newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bonds finish well bid after BOJ's Tankan survey.
newsitem.headline: NZ bonds finish well bid after BOJ's Tankan survey.

text.p: Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
FUTURES PHYSICAL YIELD
OVERNIGHT CASH 9.35 PCT (PREV 9.35) US 5-YR 5.90 (PREV 5.93)
* NZ bonds helped at close by US reaction to tankan survey
* Money market stays fairly static
* NZ First-National govt seen on the cards
New Zealand yields enjoyed a slight rally at Wednesday's close as U.S. Treasuries reacted well to the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey.
The survey showed corporate business sentiment not as strong as currency dealers had anticipated, prompting a convincing rally in the U.S. dollar.

"The New Zealand market was trading a little weakly in line with Australia and the United States earlier on in the day, but the tankan has pretty much turned that around, and there continues to be a lack of supply," one bond dealer said.
Volumes were described as patchy.
The 02/00 maturity ended three basis points lower in yield, while the 10-year bond was down two at 7.04 percent. One dealer said the 11/06 had traded to a low of seven percent.
"We were washed around in such narrow ranges -- any attempt to take it lower was generally greeted with a reasonable amount of glee," he said.

"I guess there's an expectation that the front part of the curve will continue to come lower once the green light is given," the dealer said, adding that this easing in monetary conditions was more than likely to come in the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's monetary policy statement on December 17.
The money market remained largely unchanged, with the 90-days up a basis point at 8.76 percent and the December futures contract down one at 91.58.

A Wellington dealer said yields around current levels were consistent with the emergence from coalition negotiations of either a National-New Zealand First coalition government or a minority National government.

"If either of those things were announced today, I don't think the bond market would move an inch," he said, adding that a NZ First-Labour coalition deal would be the only outcome to spark much of a market reaction.

Nationalist NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating separately with both the caretaker National Party government and the centre-left Labour Party over the shape of the next government.
